name: Rook
description: Point-trick family using the Rook deck: four colors (black, red, green, yellow), ranks 1–14 per color plus the Rook bird card. Popular in Mennonite communities and Eastern Kentucky. This entry models the common form: four in fixed partnerships, bid for nest and trump, first team to 500 wins.

content.text: Point-trick family using the Rook deck: four colors (black, red, green, yellow), ranks 1–14 per color plus the Rook bird card. Popular in Mennonite communities and Eastern Kentucky. This entry models the common form: four in fixed partnerships, bid for nest and trump, first team to 500 wins.

Rook was introduced by Parker Brothers in 1906. The deck was designed for communities that avoided standard playing cards; the game became popular in Eastern Kentucky and among Mennonites in Southern Ontario, Manitoba, Pennsylvania, and Ohio.
Four players in fixed partnerships, partners opposite.
Rook deck: four suits (colors) 1–14 each plus Rook bird card. Common variant removes 2s, 3s, 4s for 45 cards.
Ten cards each, one at a time; five cards to the nest. Dealer adds one card to the nest after each of the first five rounds of the deal.

items.text: Rook as lowest trump: Some play with the Rook as the lowest card of the trump color rather than the highest.
Point cards in nest: Some allow the bidder to discard point cards; points in the nest go to the team that wins the last trick.
Kentucky Discard: Official Rook Tournament variant: 41 cards (ones omitted), 9 each and 5 nest, dealer bids first, min bid 70, count cards may be discarded, game to 300.
Call Partner Rook: All 57 cards; bidder calls a card for partner; holder becomes partner for that hand. 13 each, 5 nest; 200 points per hand including last trick.
